about.title: Citrus Heights Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Citrus Heights sits in Sacramento County at the meeting point of several busy surface streets, and its public collision records reflect that. In 2025, the city logged 310 injury collisions, with 408 people hurt and 3 lives lost. Greenback Lane, Antelope Road, Auburn Boulevard and Sunrise Boulevard account for the largest share of reported crashes, and the numbers tend to climb on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when commuters and shoppers share the same lanes. If one of those crashes involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered. Insurers call quickly. Repair estimates and medical bills arrive out of order. LawProactive exists to take one task off your plate: finding an independent personal injury attorney who handles California car accident claims. We are not a law firm, and our service costs nothing. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened, and we make the introduction.

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California gives most car accident claims two years, but a claim involving a city vehicle or a road-maintenance issue may need to be filed within six months. The attorney you're matched with will sort out which clock applies to you.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for a collision, with your recovery reduced by your percentage of fault. Your attorney can push back on inflated fault assignments from the other side.

items.title: Nothing Owed Unless You Recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, so there is no upfront cost to get started. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in ordinary car accident cases.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my Antelope Road crash. Should I give one?
items.answer: You're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it's wise to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters can use casual phrasing to argue you were partly at fault. Instead, gather what you can: photos, the police report number, witness contacts and your medical records.

items.question: What evidence should I hang onto after a car accident in Citrus Heights?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles and the scene, the exchange-of-information sheet, any dashcam footage and your medical paperwork. Nearby businesses along corridors like Greenback Lane or Sunrise Boulevard sometimes have security cameras, but footage is often overwritten within days, so an attorney may want to send preservation requests quickly. Write down your own account while it's fresh.
